claims.text: The trip record and the trace agree that a 2.4 km booking was driven as 67.2 km. POL-RD-01 measures actual distance from the gps_trace polyline, and gps_trace.trace_distance_km (67.2 km) governs over the rounded trip_record copy; against the booked optimal of 2.4 km the derived excess is 64.8 km, or 2700% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute), and the excess is additionally MATERIAL because it exceeds 50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute, so POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is engaged.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02823, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-21T08:28:00+08:00 matches the trip_record's started_at of 2026-08-21T08:28:00+08:00, so the artifacts describe the same trip and the same pickup event. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to name a specific artifact and clause, and he names none.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes. It carries 610 fixes at a 10.0 second sampling interval with 100.0% coverage, gaps is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0, so none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 is met. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) lists; POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time refund route and POL-RD-02 governs the remedy. The surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and is 1.0, so no uplift or discount distorts the recomputation.

The vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and the 2.4 km booked optimal is the correct baseline for the POL-RD-01 test. There is no co-rider distance to exclude and no solo-optimal/matched-optimal confusion in this case.

No traffic advisory covers this corridor. EV-ADVIS-02823-01 is impaired: its admissibility status is MISSING, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT fired ('No advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window'). The absence is itself citable, and it means POL-RD-03's three-part test - named road on the optimal route, overlapping validity window, actual route leaving and rejoining the corridor - cannot be run, so no external-cause exoneration, and no closure-adjusted optimal under POL-RD-03, is available to the driver.

POL-RD-04 cannot be run in the driver's favour. Limb (a) requires an instruction from the rider recorded in the chat_log, and the chat log holds 0 messages with no first or last message timestamp, so there is no instruction, no message text from which a waypoint_hint could have been resolved, and no named road. On the clause's own terms it is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

POL-RD-05 cannot excuse any part of the excess either. The trip_record shows pickup_amended_at null, dropoff_amended_at null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so no endpoint was amended and there is no amended optimal to re-apply POL-RD-01 against. The driver's counterparty statement - 'The rider changed the destination verbally' - cites no evidence ID at all and is contradicted by the empty chat log and the absent amendment, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight and is discarded.

No mandatory escalation trigger fires, so the case can and should be ruled on this record rather than held. The identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07; the computed refund of 75.62 does not exceed SGD 150.00 and does not exceed charged_total of 83.42; there is no mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength; and no charge line lacks a counterpart (erp_lines total 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.0). Every deciding artifact carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) confidence cap is 1.0 and is above the 0.70 floor.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation is fixed by the fare_breakdown's own derived money block: recomputed_fare is 7.80 (base fare 3.80, distance 0.75 x 2.4 km = 1.80, time 0.28 x 5.0 min = 1.40, all at a surge_multiplier of 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no fixed surcharge, no waiting time and no promo). Refund_before_rounding is 75.62, the payable figure rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 is 75.65, and refund_share_of_charged is 0.9065 - 90% or more of charged_total 83.42.

Because the refund reaches 90% or more of charged_total, POL-RD-02 requires FULL_REFUND rather than a partial, and POL-GEN-03 defines FULL_REFUND as the filing party being entirely right with the whole contested amount returned - so the rider should recover the full SGD 83.42 charged. On the narrowest reading of POL-RD-02 the amount is the 75.65 payable, which is itself above the 90% line; either way the refund is far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and rounding applies only to the final payable figure.

Nothing in the pass-through layer cuts down or adds to that refund. The fare_breakdown carries no ERP gantries at all (erp_lines total 0.00, on-optimal 0.00, off-optimal 0.00), tolls of 0.0 and an airport_surcharge of 0.0 on a trip that ended at Blk 7 Everton Park and did not originate at an airport, so there is no off-route ERP to itemise separately, no double-count risk under POL-RD-09(1) and no billing-integrity line to correct under POL-RD-09(4).

The state the rider is disputing is a live charge the rider is carrying: payment_status is CHARGED, charged_total is 83.42 and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, and this dispute was filed by the RIDER. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling on a rider-filed dispute leaves that state standing, so the contested amount would simply be kept; the arithmetic refund is what moves the money back.

The rider's claim needs no corroboration beyond the trace: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so POL-RD-08's extra-corroboration condition (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not engaged and cannot be used to demand anything more than the unimpaired trace already shows.

I do not press POL-RD-06, and I say so rather than stretch it: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 210, so neither limb of the pattern test is met (neither 3 or more flags, nor a ratio of 0.05 or more on at least 40 trips), and no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) arise on this record. The rider's FULL_REFUND rests on POL-RD-02's own 90% rule, not on the driver's history.

claims.text: This trip's deviation is material on the platform's own numbers — derived.deviation.excess_km is 64.8 km and derived.deviation.excess_pct is 2700 against a 2.4 km optimal route, both far past POL-RD-01's material gates of 8.0 km / 50% — so POL-RD-06 makes the driver_profile the decisive check, and that check comes back clean: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 210. The pattern test fails on both limbs (0 is below 3, and 0/210 is below 0.05); no pattern is ESTABLISHED, so neither consequence POL-RD-06 attaches actually fires — limb (b) does not license a FULL_REFUND of charged_total on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and limb (c) does not generate a driver-conduct referral. No other counter may be substituted to repair that gap: POL-GEN-01 makes prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags, rating, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate and acceptance_rate context only, and a finding built on any of them is discarded on the same footing as an uncited claim.

The driver's account on file is that the rider changed the destination verbally. That is precisely the exculpatory route POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-05 exist to recognise, and on this record neither clause can be run in either direction: EV-CHAT-02823 carries message_count 0 and no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction test and its 200 m corroboration test have nothing to operate on, and EV-TRIP-02823 shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null with amended_optimal_distance_km null, so the amended re-quote POL-RD-05 requires does not exist in the record. These are exculpatory clauses invoked against cited artifacts that lack the fields the clauses require — the very case POL-RD-10(5) names, 'a rider-requested detour asserted with no chat_log for the trip'. The consequence is mandatory and terminal: the Judge may not issue a monetary ruling under POL-RD-02 on this record, and must ESCALATE to a human reviewer with the disputed amount held rather than collected or refunded. Whether the rider did or did not direct the change is the fact the whole dispute turns on, and no artifact in this bundle carries it.

POL-RD-13's re-reading of POL-RD-10(5) is expressly confined to a party who 'asserts an external traffic cause', and it tests that assertion 'against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else'. The driver asserts no traffic cause here, so that narrowing does not reach this case; and in any event EV-ADVIS-02823-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (impairment disclosed), so there is no advisory that could carry or defeat any traffic excuse. Nor does POL-RD-13(1)'s uncited-identifier carve-out apply, because the driver has cited the artifact POL-RD-04 requires, EV-CHAT-02823, and the clause says in terms that where the party does cite the identifier the case still escalates. The rider-instruction route through POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-05 is therefore untouched by POL-RD-13, and POL-RD-10(5) governs it as written.

The only contemporaneous record of the journey is consistent with the driver's account and contradicts nothing in it. EV-GPS-02823 is a complete, gap-free trace — 610 fixes at 10-second sampling, coverage 100%, max_gap_sec 0.0 — showing one continuous 101.5-minute run from Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 to a single drop-off at Blk 7 Everton Park, with no circling and no interrupted segment. EV-TRIP-02823 records chat_message_count 0, zero in-app calls and no cancellation; EV-CHAT-02823 confirms zero messages for the trip. A rider carried 67.2 km and 101.5 minutes through his own neighbourhood without one message, one call or a cancellation — and who first objects only the next morning, when the dispute is filed at 2026-08-22T04:06 — is at least as consistent with a destination agreed between the parties in the vehicle as with an unexplained detour, and no artifact on file says otherwise. That unresolved question is why the answer is a human reviewer and not a refund.

There is no billing defect to inflate this claim: EV-FARE-02823 itemises base fare 3.80 + distance 50.40 + time 28.42 + platform fee 0.80 = 83.42, with surge_multiplier 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, zero ERP lines, zero tolls and no airport surcharge — the ledger reconciles and the billed 67.2 km is the same figure EV-GPS-02823 records. Consequently there is no phantom line for POL-RD-09(4) to refund as a standalone correction, and no unbilled-distance shortfall against which the POL-RD-04 compensation limb could pay the driver, since the shortfall there is nil. That narrows the rider's only monetary route to the POL-RD-02 recomputation, and that route depends entirely on the exculpation and escalation questions this brief has raised — a recomputation cannot be run until it is settled whether the destination was changed at the rider's request.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver.

What happened. A ride booked as 2.4 km / 5 minutes from Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 to Blk 7 Everton Park (TRP-02823) was driven as 67.2 km in 101.5 minutes and charged SGD 83.42.

1. The deviation is established and is material. POL-RD-01 measures actual distance from the GPS polyline, and gps_trace.trace_distance_km on EV-GPS-02823 is 67.2 km — the governing figure, not the rounded copy on the trip record. Against the booked optimal of 2.4 km (EV-TRIP-02823) the excess is 64.8 km, or 2700%. Both establishment tests pass (more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km), and the excess is additionally MATERIAL (more than 50% and more than 8.0 km). The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07: 610 fixes at 10-second sampling, 100.0% coverage, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0, so the deviation stands on the trace alone and no corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

2. The driver's explanation carries no weight and is discarded. The driver's account is that the rider changed the destination verbally. It cites no evidence, and no artifact supports it. EV-CHAT-02823 is a complete chat log for this trip holding 0 messages — nothing from which a waypoint_hint could be resolved, and no road named — and EV-TRIP-02823 shows pickup_amended_at null, dropoff_amended_at null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so no endpoint was amended and no amended re-quote exists. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence carries no weight and is discarded; POL-RD-04 is unavailable on its own terms ('where waypoint_hint is null and no road is named, the corroboration test is undecidable on the record: the clause is unavailable, the case is decided on the remaining clauses'); POL-RD-05 never engages, because it is conditioned on a recorded amendment and the record shows none. The driver's separate submission that the empty record is 'consistent with a destination agreed in the vehicle' is an argument from silence and is rejected: the chat log is complete ('sequence numbering intact'), the trip record is complete, and the only thing missing from the bundle is evidence for the driver's own account.

3. Why this is not an ESCALATE. POL-RD-10(5) fires where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool, does not cover the trip window, or lacks the field the clause requires. The two artifacts the driver's side cites are neither missing nor outside the window: EV-CHAT-02823 and EV-TRIP-02823 are both present, COMPLETE and weighted 1.0.
